paper_metadata.title: Effects of an LPSO Phase Induced by Zn Addition on the High-Temperature Properties of Mg-9Gd-2Nd-(1.5Zn)-0.5Zr Alloy

evidence.quote: In this study, we prepared Mg-9Gd-2Nd-0.5Zr, referred to as alloy I, and Mg-9Gd-2Nd-1.5Zn-0.5Zr, referred to as alloy II.
The cast alloy I mainly consisted of an α-Mg matrix and a Mg5RE phase. After adding Zn, the Mg5RE phase in the cast alloy transformed into a (Mg,Zn)3RE phase

parameters.atmosphere: SF6 and CO2 protective gas (volume ratio 1:99)

evidence.quote: The temperature was raised to 720 ◦C and maintained for 30 min. After completely melting the pure magnesium, the temperature was raised to 780 ◦C, and the Mg-30Gd intermediate alloy was added into the crucible. After melting sufficiently, the temperature was reduced to 750 ◦C, and the Mg-30Nd and Mg-30Zr intermediate alloys were added and maintained for 30 min. The melt was poured into a mold and then cooled to 25 ◦C. Finally, alloy I was obtained.

parameters.atmosphere: SF6 and CO2 protective gas (volume ratio 1:99)

evidence.quote: Under the above conditions, it was cooled to 730 ◦C, and pure Zn was added for another 30 min to complete the preparation of alloy II.
Alloy I was first kept at 525 ◦C for 5 h for a solid solution treatment, and then quenched in water at a temperature of 25 ◦C.

parameters.cooling_method: furnace cooling to 400 °C then water quenching

evidence.quote: In order to obtain the LPSO phase, alloy II was first kept at 525 ◦C for 4 h, and then cooled down to 400 ◦C in the furnace. It remained for 4 h at 400 ◦C, followed by water quenching and cooling.
Then, water-quenched alloy I and alloy II samples were subjected to an aging treatment. They were kept at 250 ◦C for 4 h and then air-cooled to room temperature.

alloy I consisted of an α-Mg matrix (the black area) and an irregular strip-shaped secondary phase (the white area) widely distributed along the grain boundaries

energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) analysis of the white area revealed that it was primarily composed of Mg, Gd, and Nd, with an atomic (Gd+Nd)/Mg ratio close to 1:5, indicating that it was a Mg5RE(Gd,Nd) phase. The volume fraction statistics of the white area showed that it accounted for 6.6% of the total volume.
alloy II consisted of an α-Mg matrix, and the secondary phase was distributed along the grain boundary in a semi-continuous mesh-like shape

EDS analysis of the secondary phase showed that it was mainly composed of Mg, Zn, Gd, and Nd, with an atomic (Gd + Nd)/(Mg+Zn) ratio close to 1:3, indicating that it was a (Mg,Zn)3RE(Gd,Nd) phase. The volume fraction statistics of the secondary phase showed that it accounted for 9.4% of the total volume.

evidence.quote: the semi-continuous network-like secondary phase ((Mg,Zn)3RE) at the crystal boundary of the as-cast alloy II was not completely dissolved but transformed into discontinuous small blocks. According to the EDS results in Figure 3c, the small needle-like phase was still (Mg,Zn) 3RE.

evidence.section: 3.4. Effects of the LPSO Phase on the Tensile Properties

evidence.section: 3.4. Effects of the LPSO Phase on the Tensile Properties
evidence.quote: with the increase in temperature, the atomic reactivity in the crystals was enhanced, making atomic diffusion migration more likely to occur. This resulted in an increase in the vacancy density, leading to a decrease in strength.
